item.title: Shota Imanaga's home run struggles and Wrigley wind make over 7.5 the play for Braves-Cubs
item.description: JR Ritchie faces Shota Imanaga as the Atlanta Braves and Chicago Cubs clash in what could be a playoff preview with wind playing a key factor.
item.content:encoded:
This late in the season, there are a few types of series: one that doesn't matter at all because neither team will make the postseason. Another is between one team that is still battling for the postseason.

Then there are those between two teams trying to make the playoffs or solidify their position. And, finally, there is one between two teams that are essentially locked into making the postseason, but maybe not the exact spot. That's what we have tonight between the Atlanta Braves and the Chicago Cubs, perhaps a preview of a playoff series.

The Braves are one of the more consistent teams in baseball this season. They've been one of the best teams in the sport all year, and since opening day, they've positioned themselves as the division leader. I believe they may have lost it for a stretch when the Philadelphia Phillies were hot, but the point remains that this is one of the more complete and best teams in baseball. However, they do have a weakness: road games. They are above .500 on the road, but being 26 games above .500 overall, the majority of that is their home record.

There really isn't a question about whether the Braves will make the postseason; they just need to lock up the division, and they currently have a 5.5-game lead. Looking to push that division lead further is today's starter, JR Ritchie. For the season, Ritchie is 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA and a 1.43 WHIP. He really doesn't have significantly different home and road splits. However, he does have a 5.13 ERA in night games compared to 3.06 on the road. Ritchie has pitched better lately, but doesn't go too deep into games. The Cubs haven't seen much of him and are hitting just .167 against Ritchie.

The Cubs have also held strong with their position for much of the season. They've never really been able to overtake the Brewers in the NL Central, but they've been in control of the first Wild Card spot for much of the year. If you gave the Cubs a better rotation, they probably would be the World Series favorite, or at least up there with the Dodgers. The offense has carried this team for much of the year, specifically Pete Crow-Armstrong.

The pitching staff has been the major problem this season. There have been a variety of injuries, but there are also just poor performances as the Cubs have given up more homers than any other staff in the National League. One of those guys who has struggled with the long ball is Shota Imanaga. He takes the ball tonight and has already allowed 34 homers this season. The good news for him is that he doesn't allow a lot of hits or walks, but he does allow a lot of homers. He had a stellar July, but struggled in August. His September has been good so far. He faced Atlanta once this season and allowed just two earned runs over seven innings of work.

The wind is a major factor at Wrigley, but if Imanaga is not on his game, hitters can still blast the ball out of the park. Ritchie isn't a guy I have a ton of confidence in on the mound either. item.title: ‘Worse than Watergate’ New FBI files detail agent’s push to join Trump probe, investigate Elon Musk
item.description: Chuck Grassley released FBI emails from Crossfire Hurricane, calling Obama and Biden administration operations against Trump worse than Watergate.
item.content:encoded:
Senate Judiciary Committee Chair Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, released a batch of unclassified emails between FBI agents stemming from Operation Crossfire Hurricane, a Justice Department investigation launched during the Obama administration into whether then-presidential candidate Donald Trump's campaign was colluding with Russia during the 2016 election.

Grassley argued that the email exchanges, which included former FBI Special Agent Kevin Gounaud seeking to open an investigation into Elon Musk over the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), revealed that the "Deep State" was at work to undermine Trump.

"The previous Democrat administrations under Obama and Biden conducted secret, insidious and downright evil operations that almost took down our government," Grassley said during an Oversight hearing with FBI Director Kash Patel. "That's arguably worse than Watergate."

DAN BONGINO REVEALS HE FOUND 'MOTHER LODE' OF SECRET RUSSIAGATE FILES INSIDE FBI BURN BAGS

Over the past decade, the Senate Judiciary Committee, at the direction of Grassley, has released several rounds of documents from a few FBI operations such as Operation Arctic Frost and Round River, alleging that the Justice Department was being weaponized against Trump and Republicans.

"The overall sustained efforts by the Deep State in the dark corners of the bureaucracy is worse than anything Trump has been accused of. At least he’s upfront and open so people can judge," Grassley said.

At the center of the Senate Judiciary Committee's most recent document release are three former FBI agents: Gounaud, Walter Giardina, who was fired by Patel in August over accusations of political weaponization, and Timothy Thibault.

Gounaud, who left the bureau in February, according to his LinkedIn, sent an email in February 2025 seeking to begin a criminal investigation of Musk. At the time, Musk was a special government employee overseeing DOGE. Gounaud's complaint centered on Musk announcing on X his plan to have all government employees share five things they worked on that day.

"Musk used a non government system (twitter) to relate information that allegedly was for official purposes. In doing so, because he is monetized (he is a majority owner of twitter) he likely generated income for himself based on Twitter's monetization model and/or advertising revenues," Gounaud wrote. "His use of twitter in this and other instances is conceptually similar to Hillary Clinton's misuse of a private email server for government business."

Grassley later criticized the former FBI agent in a post on X.

JACK SMITH'S SENATE PHONE RECORDS PROBE TURNS TO VERIZON'S HANDLING OF SUBPOENAS

"Here is an email I released 2day showing an FBI agent who was ready2 open a CRIMINAL CASE all bc Elon Musk asked govt bureaucrats 2 report 5 things they did in a wk," Grassley wrote. "Compare that 2 Iowans who work frm sunup to sundown EVERY DAY Washington rlly is an island surrounded by reality."

The document dump also shows that Giardina emailed at least seven times over the course of four weeks beginning in January 2017 asking to be assigned to Crossfire Hurricane. The findings of the investigation were handed off to special counsel Robert Mueller a few months later in May.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The emails show that Giardina was in correspondence with Thibault, who Grassley had accused of violating the Hatch Act. The allegation, which was investigated and dismissed by the U.S. Office of Special Counsel (OSC), stemmed from Thibault resharing a post on then Twitter by the Lincoln Project, which called Trump a "psychologically broken, embittered, and deeply unhappy man."

Thibault is included in several emails sent by Giardina to former Supervising Agent Joe Pientka.

"Based on the records known to date, that case didn’t advance," Grassley said. "His efforts, as well as the case he tried to open on Senator Sinema, undercut public statements by former FBI officials that agents don’t get to pick their cases."

item.title: 5 states could be the biggest losers in Trump's trade war with Canada, expert warns
item.description: President Donald Trump's trade war with Canada exposes $2.3 billion in Ohio exports to retaliatory tariffs ahead of the critical midterm elections.
item.content:encoded:
Americans' pocketbooks could take yet another hit ahead of the November election as President Donald Trump escalates his trade war with Canada — with five key battleground states likely facing the most fallout.

Billions of dollars in U.S. exports are exposed to the northern neighbor's retaliatory tariffs that target American goods across a range of industries. The outcome? Costs are expected to continue rising for U.S. businesses and consumers in the weeks leading to the must-win midterms.

Affordability remains a prominent issue for voters, while tariffs remain a cornerstone of Trump's economic agenda. He claims the strategy will result in more domestic manufacturing and pressure trade partners into agreements that are more beneficial for American industries and consumers. But the result so far has been an increase in prices for the average American family.

"American manufacturers or American businesses who rely on Canadian inputs are going to start to feel the pain right in the lead up to going to the ballot box," David Clement, policy director of the free market nonprofit Consumer Choice Center, told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED

Clement identified Ohio, Illinois, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin as among the states most exposed to negative fallout, based on their current trade with Canada and the goods targeted by the tariffs.

"Ohio is by far the most vulnerable state in terms of exposure from the Canadian retaliatory tariffs," Clement said, estimating roughly $2.3 billion in exports to Canada are exposed.

He pointed to machinery, transportation products, minerals and metals as major sources of that vulnerability.

In Michigan, the impact is particularly evident in the auto industry, where supply chains are deeply intertwined with neighboring Ontario.

"Most Americans don’t know that a single component on a U.S.-assembled vehicle can cross the border upwards of eight times before it’s actually completed," Clement said.

"When you are tariffing automotive parts going across the border each way," he added, "it really gums up the very intertwined supply chain for cars between Michigan and Ontario."

A FRESH MIDTERM HEADACHE FOR THE GOP JUST HIT A NATIONAL RECORD

Those costs can eventually make their way to consumers, Clement argued.

Pennsylvania also faces significant exposure. Clement said about 25% of the state's exports go to Canada, much of it machinery and equipment, putting just under $1.8 billion in exports at risk.

What the trade fight means politically is less certain. Clement argued that even a change in congressional control after November would not necessarily bring the tariffs to an end.

A POPULAR COCKTAIL HAS A TRUMP TRADE PROBLEM YOU PROBABLY DIDN’T KNOW ABOUT

"The idea that Canadian retaliatory tariffs are going to swing the midterms in the Democrats’ favor and then all of a sudden create an end to the trade war is a fantasy," Clement said.

He cited the legislative hurdles to reversing presidential trade policy and noted that the Biden administration kept a number of tariffs imposed during Trump's first term.

Still, Clement argued the timing could matter, with Canada's retaliatory tariffs already in place as the midterms approach.

"Cost of living, cost of goods, cost of doing business is such an important factor for Americans who are going to be casting a ballot," he said.

item.title: Dem fundraising giant ActBlue accused of fraudulent donation 'cover-up' in explosive report
item.description: ActBlue allegedly weakened fraud prevention twice in 2024, with internal memos showing supervisors green-lighting donations despite red flags.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: A Democrat fundraising giant used by the biggest players on the left is being accused of covering up the acceptance of fraudulent political donations and lying to Congress about its security standards.

Congressional Republicans are providing an update on their investigation of ActBlue — a platform for campaigns to raise money that's used by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and the Democratic leaders of the House and Senate, among others — that alleges the company potentially accepted foreign contributions and concealed the evidence from the GOP's probe.

ActBlue has previously denied any wrongdoing.

DEM FUNDRAISING GIANT IN THE HOT SEAT AS GOP LAWMAKERS DEMAND ANSWERS OVER DODGED SUBPOENA

"The Committees’ oversight has found that ActBlue, in its own words, decided to take 'a more lenient approach' to fraud prevention in 2024, weakening its fraud-prevention policies at least twice even though internal assessments showed that these changes would result in a measurable increase in fraudulent contributions," the report said, citing an ActBlue staff report.

"Similarly, internal trainings directed ActBlue’s fraud prevention team to 'look for reasons to accept contributions' rather than to examine them closely for indicators of fraud — as required by federal regulation. ActBlue took this lax approach to fraud prevention even though it had detected at least 22 significant fraud campaigns on the platform in recent years, including several from foreign sources."

Republicans accused ActBlue of accepting "illegal foreign political donations" and the "subsequent cover-up" of that information.

As an example, the report cited a letter by ActBlue CEO Regina Wallace-Jones to Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis., which maintained that donations on the platform made by people with addresses outside the U.S. required a passport number for verification.

KEY HOUSE COMMITTEE SCHEDULES HEARING WITH EMBATTLED ACTBLUE CEO: 'NEEDS TO COME CLEAN'

But Republicans alleged that the verification "only ensures that the entered passport number contains a certain number of characters, not that it is a valid U.S. passport number," rendering it an essentially meaningless step.

The report also included excerpts purporting to show ActBlue supervisors green-lighting donations despite "red flags," including a memo lauding a donation as a "great accept" but noting, "Donor sometimes has an IP in Hong Kong, but none of their other signals raise any eyebrows."

Another communication appears to show an ActBlue supervisor maintaining that a denied contribution "should have been accepted." The rest of the memo stated, "It is a foreign contribution, but the name/email match, the IP/billing match, a full address with the correct country code, and there were previously accepted and successful contributions."

"The donor uses an Arkansas state code, which isn’t great, but [the] system can be wonky with requiring state codes for foreign donors," the rest of the message stated.

FIRST ON FOX: ACTBLUE BOARD MEMBERS IN HOT SEAT AS GOP PROBES 'SERIOUS' MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS

An ActBlue supervisor also allegedly said a contribution "set off a lot of" alarms but argued the donor should be given the "benefit of the doubt."

The communications excerpts were included in the report and not independently verified by Fox News Digital.

ACTBLUE SUES TEXAS AG KEN PAXTON, ALLEGING POLITICAL RETALIATION OVER DEMOCRATS' FUNDRAISING

But despite the GOP's accusations, the report's evidence also appears to show ActBlue employees standing by the platform.

An email from ActBlue employees shows they believe the company to be "the target of bad-faith political attacks at the hands of ill-intentioned operators."

ActBlue also previously told the committee "there is no evidence that foreign donations through online or small-dollar contributions are a problem in U.S. elections."

Despite the pushback in print, multiple ActBlue leaders who have appeared before Congress have opted to invoke the Fifth Amendment to avoid testifying.

HOUSE DEM LASHES OUT AT GOP EFFORTS TO PROBE FOREIGN DONATIONS WITH STUNNING CLAIM ON MOTIVE

The probe is being led by Steil alongside House Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, and House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky.

Democrats have denounced the investigation as a cynical effort to undermine faith in U.S. elections. But Republicans argued that it's an effort to enhance that confidence by rooting out potential fraud.

Fox News Digital reached out to ActBlue for a response to the report.

item.title: Injured Louisiana boy hailed a 'superhero' for seeking help during deadly stabbing rampage
item.description: A 6-year-old Houma, Louisiana, boy fled to a neighbor's door after a mass stabbing that killed four Verret family members before passing out inside.
item.content:encoded:
A 6-year-old boy from Houma, Louisiana, is being hailed as a "superhero" for escaping a mass stabbing that left four dead, making it to a neighbor's doorstep and passing out inside the house after suffering stab wounds that landed him in the hospital.

The suspect, Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, reportedly followed the boy to the neighbor's door, knocked him to the ground and then fled. Once the boy got into the house, he lost consciousness, according to local WWL, and the neighbor called 911.

Solet was also hospitalized for injuries that took place during the alleged mass stabbing. He was released from the hospital on Tuesday and booked on four counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted first-degree murder, according to the Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office.

MAN ACCUSED IN BRUTAL MOTEL STABBING SOUGHT AS PERSON OF INTEREST IN 4 DEATHS, CHILD ATTACK

The boy is "stable" after suffering multiple stab wounds, his father wrote Tuesday in a Facebook post.

"Please pray for my little man as he recovers he’s so so strong and such a fighter," the father wrote. "Current status (he’s stable) thank everybody for reaching out."

"I just wanna thank everybody for the prayers I’m trying to tell everyone thank you it’s just a lot right now," the boy's father wrote on X, sharing memorials that describe her son as a "superhero" and mourn the loss of four family members, adding his son "appreciates every last one of you reaching out and helping and praying."

DAYCARE OPERATOR ARRESTED AFTER 3-YEAR-OLD WAS LEFT UNCONSCIOUS IN POOL FOR 20 MINUTES, DIED

"I told him earlier that he has so many people behind him and praying for him and he smiled thank yall fr , god bless."

The Terrebonne Sheriff's Office captured Solet early Sunday morning after a manhunt aided by the boy and the neighbor.

"On September 12, 2026, Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office Deputies responded to the 200 block of Ashland Drive, where they located a juvenile suffering from apparent stab wounds," a sheriff's office Facebook post read. "The juvenile was transported by Acadian Ambulance Service Air Med to an out-of-area hospital in critical condition.

"As Deputies continued their preliminary investigation, four deceased victims were discovered inside two nearby residences. Detectives were called in to assist, and began processing multiple scenes, gathering evidence, interviewing witnesses, and developing information surrounding the incidents. During the investigation, Detectives identified Solet as a person of interest and began an intensive effort to locate him."

There was a GoFundMe set up for the boy and his family. The crowdfunding page identified the boy's relatives Verna Mae Verdin and Letha Verret as victims who were killed in their home during the attack. That page had reached almost $60,000 of the $70,000 goal as of Wednesday morning.

"Despite his injuries, he was able to escape and get help," organizer Brandon Thiel said of the 6-year-old survivor. "He is currently in critical condition at a local hospital, where he continues to fight for his life. This devastating tragedy has left the Verret family facing an unimaginable amount of grief, uncertainty, and hardship. The loss is especially profound for Letha’s minor children, who are now having to cope with the sudden loss of their mother, grandmother, and uncle all at once."

ICE BOSTON ARRESTS BRAZILIAN ILLEGAL ALIEN WANTED FOR MURDER DAYS BEFORE GOV HEALY SIGNED PROTECT ACT

Solet reportedly was known to the family, and the sheriff's reports shared no motive.

"Our hearts remain with the victims, their families and every member of our community who has been affected by this unimaginable tragedy," Sheriff Tim Soignet wrote in a statement posted to Facebook. "We recognize that no words can lessen the pain these families are experiencing, but we want them to know that they are not alone and that our agency remains firmly committed to pursuing justice on their behalf.

"I am incredibly proud of our personnel and supporting agencies whose immediate response and tireless work brought this investigation to this point. Our Deputies are members of this community, and they carry the weight of these tragedies alongside the families and citizens we serve."

The latest investigation is not the first time Solet’s name has surfaced in violent crime allegations.

Solet was arrested in December 2019 for allegedly stabbing a woman repeatedly and leaving her locked inside a Houma motel room, according to a police news release from the time.

Asked why Solet was no longer in custody, Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office Lt. Blake Tabor said authorities were also searching for answers.

"I can’t tell you. Certainly, that’s the hot question, right? Why is he out?" Tabor said. "We’re probably just as stunned as everyone else is."

Tabor emphasized that the sheriff’s office has a strong working relationship with the Terrebonne Parish District Attorney’s Office but said questions remain about how Solet’s previous cases were handled.

"How this slipped through, I certainly don’t know, but it’s a question that probably needs to be answered," Tabor said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the district attorney’s office seeking the circumstances surrounding Solet’s release and whether he remained under any court-ordered supervision but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: WWE legend Rey Mysterio shares his thoughts on celebrities and pro athletes entering pro wrestling space
item.description: Rey Mysterio says WWE celebrity crossovers with Jason Kelce and Bad Bunny are fun, revealing how stars realize wrestling is real in the ring.
item.content:encoded:
WWE has been able to cross over to mainstream sports and entertainment over the last few years with stars from all over stepping inside the ring – Jason Kelce, Bad Bunny, Jelly Roll, Ryan Garcia, Mike Mathews, Cam Skattebo and Lil Yachty, to name a few.

Even Tom Brady said he would consider a storyline in WWE before getting in the face of Logan Paul and attempting to slap the wrestler. But some fans, in the year of 2026, have grown tired of the mixing between celebrities and professional wrestling.

WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio told OutKick Dropkick ahead of Triplemania Night 1 in Las Vegas that he doesn’t mind the mix.

"I really don’t mind it at all. We always had celebrities pop into our world and maybe they were fans prior, maybe they weren’t fans and they came over and they saw our craft, they respected it," he said. "But overall, I think it’s always fun and cool to have collaborations from celebrities jumping on over to our craft as well as us to their craft, their sport, whatever it is that they’re doing. That makes things much more interesting. We engage with much more fans and I think that’s the goal of it all – to get as many eyes as possible."

item.title: Jim Jordan subpoenas blue state DAs accused of 'preferential treatment' for illegal immigrant criminals
item.description: Jim Jordan issued subpoenas to district attorneys in Fairfax County and Boulder County, accusing both of giving preferential treatment to criminal aliens.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, is ratcheting up his crackdown against sanctuary jurisdictions across the country.

Jordan is sending subpoenas to district attorneys in Boulder, Colorado, and Fairfax, Virginia, accusing both of giving "preferential treatment" to "criminal aliens" when weighing whether and how to prosecute wrongdoing.

"Despite repeated requests for responsive documents and communications, you have not produced a single document. Accordingly, because you have failed to comply with the Committee’s requests, the Committee is serving compulsory process," he wrote in separate letters to Fairfax County Commonwealth’s Attorney Steve Descano and Boulder County District Attorney Michael Dougherty, both obtained by Fox News Digital.

HOCHUL BOASTS 'I JUST BANNED IT' AS NEW YORK OUTLAWS LOCAL POLICE PARTNERSHIPS WITH ICE

"Your office’s lenient treatment of foreign national criminals endangers communities and ensures that criminal aliens escape both criminal and immigration accountability for their actions."

Jordan's committee has for weeks investigated district attorneys who have been accused of taking immigration status into account when pursuing criminal complaints, even when the alleged crime has nothing to do with the suspect's legal status.

DOJ OPENS INVESTIGATION INTO SOROS-BACKED DA ACCUSED OF SHIELDING ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS FROM CONSEQUENCES

Descano, in particular, has recently made headlines after the stabbing death of 41-year-old U.S. citizen Stephanie Minter, whose accused killer came to the U.S. illegally from Sierra Leone in 2012. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said the man had been arrested over 30 times before Minter's killing.

item.title: Trump DHS hits 16 straight months with 0 releases at the border
item.description: President Donald Trump's border policies hit 16 consecutive months of zero releases as apprehensions dropped 94% from Biden-era averages.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX – President Donald Trump's administration marked 16 consecutive months of making zero releases at the U.S.-Mexican border on Wednesday.

The Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Customs and Border Protection announced the unprecedented record in a statement to Fox News Digital. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the streak proves that President Donald Trump's policies "are working."

"Catch and release is over, consequences are back, and illegal crossings have fallen to historic lows. President Trump made a promise to the American people that he would make America safe again, and he has done just that by giving us the most secure border in American history," Mullin said.

"Border security starts with knowing who and what is entering our country – and controlling it on behalf of the American people," said CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott. "That means people who cross illegally are apprehended, detained and removed – not released into the United States. Our agents are enforcing that standard every day."

TRUMP HITS DRAMATIC MILESTONE IN MASSIVE DEPARTURE FROM BIDEN BORDER PLAN: 'WHAT A DIFFERENCE'

U.S. Border Patrol said it apprehended 8,870 people along the Southwest border in August, which is 5% lower than July.

The August apprehension numbers were 94% lower than the average month under former President Joe Biden. DHS also says it made zero parole releases in August, compared to the Border Patrol releasing over 10,000 in August 2024 under Biden.

Other law enforcement numbers at the border remain strong as well, with fiscal year drug seizures up 73% compared to the same fiscal period under Biden in 2024. Drug seizures are also up 61% compared to the average of the past four years.

CBP OFFICERS SEIZE $67 MILLION IN ILLEGAL DRUGS AT SAN DIEGO BORDER PORTS, DHS SAYS

The rise in drug seizures comes largely from cocaine and precursor chemicals. Cocaine seizures increased 28% in August to 6,724 pounds, while CBP and ICE seized over 120,000 pounds of precursor chemicals in the same month.

The August numbers come the same month the Trump administration began construction of a section of a border wall in Arizona despite objections from a Native American tribe.

MULLIN TELLS CONGRESS PRIMARY BORDER WALL WILL BE DONE BY JUNE 2027, SECONDARY WALL BY SUMMER 2028

The wall is part of a $46 billion effort to shore up the southern border with 30-foot steel bollard walls, vehicle barriers and technology designed to stop illegal immigration and smuggling.

However, the Tohono O'odham Nation sued the administration earlier this year, saying the construction will damage land sacred to the tribe.

A federal judge rejected the argument, siding with the government and noting that the border wall would be built on a 60-foot-wide buffer zone of federally owned land called the Roosevelt Reservation.

"Defendants have not yet articulated plans to construct outside the Roosevelt Reservation," U.S. District Judge Richard Leon in Washington, D.C., wrote in his opinion.

Fox News' Peter D'Abrosca and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Florida woman allegedly drugs man she met at club, steals his nearly $100K Rolex: police
item.description: Lynda Mae Crouse allegedly drugged a man she met at a South Florida club before stealing his $98,400 diamond-bedazzled Rolex Presidential watch.
item.content:encoded:
A woman was arrested after allegedly meeting a man at a club in South Florida, going home with him and drugging him before stealing his nearly $100,000 Rolex watch, according to court records.

Lynda Mae Crouse, 32, is accused of using a similar scheme at least four other times in Miami-Dade County, allegedly drugging victims before making off with their valuables, according to a probable cause affidavit.

The Broward County case she is being charged for stems from an April 12 encounter at the Carousel Club in Hallandale Beach, where Crouse allegedly struck up a conversation with the man around midnight.

The two exchanged Instagram accounts and parted ways before the man later sent an Uber to Crouse's home around 1:20 a.m. to bring her to his residence, police said.

MIAMI WOMAN ALLEGEDLY LURED MAN TO LUXURY CONDO VIA INSTAGRAM, THEN ROBBED HIM WITH 2 ACCOMPLICES

Crouse and the unidentified man had several alcoholic drinks in his living room before he went into his bedroom to change clothes. While there, he suddenly began feeling "funny" and "extremely tired," according to the affidavit.

While Crouse was alone in the living room, the man said he heard a distinctive "clapping sound." When he returned, Crouse was "acting different" and abruptly announced she was going home. Within minutes of her leaving, he fell asleep.

When the man awoke several hours later still feeling strange, he remembered the sound and rushed to check his Rolex box in the living room. His gold 40 mm diamond-bedazzled Rolex Presidential was gone.

DRINK-SPIKING DEFENSE: NEW BRACELET AIMS TO EXPOSE DRUGS WITH A DROP OF YOUR COCKTAIL

The man later provided police with an appraisal valuing the watch at $98,400. He also identified Crouse in a photo lineup, according to the affidavit.

Months later, on Friday, Sept. 11, 2026, Crouse was arrested by Seminole police and taken to Broward County Jail.

She was charged with second-degree grand theft, a felony, and released the following day after posting $2,500 bond.

In another case investigated by City of Miami police, Crouse was accused of drugging a victim with zolpidem, a prescription sleep aid used to treat insomnia.

Unlike the Broward County victim, that person underwent toxicology testing, which confirmed the presence of zolpidem.

item.title: Dem House speaker torched for invoking 9/11 to attack key Trump policy: 'Totally wrong'
item.description: Ryan Mackenzie demands Joanna McClinton apologize after the Pennsylvania House speaker linked Trump's immigration crackdown to potential 9/11 violence.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Ryan Mackenzie, R-Pa., fired back at the Pennsylvania House speaker, a Democrat, after she suggested the Trump administration’s crackdown on illegal immigration could invite 9/11-like violence.

"She used her time to actually denounce securing our border and saying that, somehow, the efforts to keep our country safe could lead to another attack," Mackenzie told Fox News Digital.

"She’s totally wrong. She’s answering to the far-left radicals and globalists. I would actually call on Joanna McClinton to apologize for what she said at that event," he added.

McClinton’s criticism highlights a challenge Democrats face as they search for vulnerabilities in Trump’s immigration agenda: attacking the administration’s aggressive enforcement tactics even as illegal border crossings have fallen sharply.

DEM REP SETH MOULTON SAYS PARTY HAS NO IMMIGRATION PLAN, IS ONLY ‘OPPOSITION TO TRUMP’

Speaking at a panel discussion on the 250th anniversary of American independence, McClinton said she feared the threat of retaliation for Trump’s "brutality."

"When we think of just the brutality of this federal government for almost two years, it’s been heartless. It’s been too silent on the other side of the aisle. They are treating people with no respect or dignity — people who came here to do better. It’s horrible. So, when we think about where we are in 2026 and that it’s been 25 years, thank God we have not had another attack," McClinton said.

"Thank God we haven’t seen another plane go down in Pennsylvania. But we also have to recognize that our policies are impacting our perception around the world," McClinton added.

McClinton first became speaker in the Pennsylvania House in 2023 and first joined the chamber in 2015. Before her time in politics, she worked as a public defender.

McClinton has voiced similar criticisms of immigration enforcement before, framing Trump’s use of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as a tool that has gone too far.

DEMOCRAT COMPARES ICE TO 'DOMESTIC TERRORISTS' AS 111 HOUSE DEMS DEMAND TEXAS DETENTION CENTER CLOSE

Completely horrified by ICE agents so brutally hunting down, harming people every day – and now using deadly force!!!! God have mercy," McClinton wrote in a post to X, referring to deadly encounters between ICE and protesters earlier this year.

Since Trump returned to office, illegal border crossings have sunk to historic lows. Since the end of 2024, encounters have gone from 144,000 in December 2024 to just 33,800 in July — a reduction of 76.5%.

Mackenzie believes Democrats like McClinton are ignoring that record.

"What she should be doing is making sure that we’re protecting and defending American citizens in our country at every single turn," Mackenzie said.

SHAPIRO VS TRUMP-BACKED GARRITY SET FOR HIGH-STAKES PENNSYLVANIA GOVERNOR SHOWDOWN

In addition to demanding an apology from McClinton, Mackenzie also called on other Democrats, like his own congressional opponent, to condemn her thinking.

"My opponent in the congressional race, Bob Brooks, should condemn that kind of rhetoric. We need to make sure that we are always pushing back on these types of things that are really inappropriate and being said by Democrat leaders who are trying to push their radical agenda instead of doing what is right for our country," Mackenzie said.

McClinton’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Trump’s beef import scheme wreaks havoc on fed-up red state cattle ranchers
item.description: Cattle ranchers in red states say Trump's 300,000 metric ton beef import plan has caused market volatility and cost them significant money per head.
item.content:encoded:
As the Trump administration desperately tries to cut costs for Americans ahead of November's midterm elections, one critical demographic to U.S. food supplies is becoming increasingly fed up.

President Donald Trump in August announced that the U.S. would import 300,000 metric tons of foreign beef trim, well over half a billion pounds, from nations around the world, leaving some cattle ranchers in red states typically aligned with the president's agenda uneasy heading into a high-stakes election for Republicans.

"These markets have been very volatile the last month," Greg Gunthorp, a farm-to-table cattle farmer in northeast Indiana, told Fox News Digital. "The ranchers have lost a lot of equity. The markets are down substantially."

‘WHY WOULD HE DO THIS TO US?’: TRUMP'S FOREIGN BEEF PUSH IS HURTING HIS BASE, REPUBLICANS WARN

Gunthorp said the current uncertainty makes it difficult to decide whether to retain heifers for breeding or sell them as feeder cattle. Complicating matters is the fact that cattle herds in the U.S. have already thinned to their lowest level in 75 years, which could spell disaster for ranchers and consumers. Part of that shortage stems from a prolonged drought that has decimated some of the Midwest herd populations.

Additionally, spiking diesel costs stemming from the war in Iran means cattle ranchers are already operating on thinner margins and being forced to raise their prices.

Jaclyn Wilson, a cattle rancher in western Nebraska, told Fox News Digital that how much of the 300,000 metric tons is actually imported, another unanswered question, is critical to assessing the impact that the Trump administration's move will have on the industry.

TRUMP WANTS CHEAPER BEEF. REPUBLICANS IN KEY RACES WARN HIS PLAN GOES TOO FAR

"The only thing that really concerns me and continues to concern me, is that the market volatility is definitely there," she said.

"It seems like any time that we have significant prices in the beef industry and our administration says something, we do see that market fluctuate and that can be devastating for producers that are selling calves right now or even yearling," Wilson continued.

Wilson said she sold some yearling steers just after the announcement was made, and got $175 less per head than she would have normally.

"And that's pretty significant for a producer," she said.

Another common theme shared by ranchers who spoke with Fox News Digital is that they want the government to incentivize producing cattle, or at least stay out of the market and let cattle ranchers do it on their own.

BROOKE ROLLINS, MONICA CROWLEY: AMERICA’S FAMILY FARMS HAVE KEPT US STRONG FOR 250 YEARS

"You can relieve a price temporarily today, but they're not going to put cattle back in Mississippi pastures," said Mississippi cattle rancher Mary Jo Perry. "And that's the problem, is that we have a cattle shortage. So, something needs to be done to encourage farmers and incentivize them, enable them to retain heifers."

Perry, who runs a grass-fed, farm-to-table beef operation, said the White House's policy proposal hasn't affected her business. She sells beef to health-conscious customers who want to know that their food is high quality and that their beef was raised without feeding on corn or soy.

Wilson would just as much prefer the government to stay out the business altogether.

"I think that's what's so discouraging for me as a cattle producer is that I'm trying to do what my family has done for generations, and somebody else is dictating it right now, she said. "I'm not given those opportunities to make that choice, and that's what's really disappointing."

NEBRASKA RANCHERS STRUGGLE TO RECOVER FROM HISTORIC WILDFIRES AS DROUGHT WORSENS CRISIS

"We talk about herd rebuilding, and that's something this administration is also talked about — which I agree, we do need to rebuild our cowherd — but keep the government out of it," she said. "Let it naturally happen. Mother Nature, of course, is the biggest component of that."

Fox News Digital spoke with Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins at the GOP Midterm Convention in Dallas last week about the cattle ranching conundrum.

The secretary said she's spoken with "hundreds and hundreds" of cattle ranchers to explain Trump's thinking in importing beef.

"So, hearing from those ranchers directly was really important," Rollins said. "But what we did — and we've already done a whole lot of pro-rancher stuff a year ago — battling for private property rights, taking out the weaponization that the left had put in against our ranchers [and] working to take their land away ... so all of that was already in motion."

TRUMP ADMIN SCRAPS ‘WEAPONIZED’ WILDLIFE RULE THAT BECAME 'BURDEN' ON AMERICAN FAMILIES AND BUSINESSES: BURGUM

"But what that decision, as frustrated as our ranchers were, what that decision allowed was really an opportunity for us at USDA and also work across the cabinet — which this Cabinet is very unusual in that way — to put together the most pro-rancher agenda in American history," she continued.

"Until President Trump took office, America’s ranchers were treated as a problem with policy geared toward their eventual extinction. The consequences were devastating: a war on beef, a cattle herd at a 75-year low, and the loss of tens of thousands of family operations," said Rollins told Fox News Digital. "President Trump promised to put the American ranchers first, and the Ranchers First Initiative delivers on that promise. We are investing real dollars to rebuild the Great American Beef Herd, giving producers the risk management tools they need, cutting the red tape that has squeezed small and independent operators, and demanding transparency in a marketplace that has been consolidated and foreign-owned for far too long. President Trump will make certain the men and women who raise our cattle can hand their operations to the next generation, and that American families can put safe, high-quality, American-raised beef on the table."

On Sept. 4, 2026, Trump signed two executive orders related to cattle ranchers and beef production. One, "Supporting America's Ranchers," is aimed at strengthening the cattle industry by ordering federal agencies to cut red tape and regulations, expand cattle grazing and look into predator management. The latter will determine whether certain species of wolves that prey on cattle have grown enough to be delisted from endangered species lists.

On the same day, he signed another order focused on meat processing and market competition. It demands stricter enforcement of the Packers and Stockyards Act against unfair, deceptive or monopolistic practices in the livestock industry, along with expanding opportunities to sell meat across state lines through cooperative meat safety inspections.

"President Trump has repeatedly affirmed his support for America’s great farmers and ranchers," White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told Fox News Digital. "While the Administration is addressing a short-term supply crunch in the beef market, we are simultaneously working closely with ranchers to grow America’s cattle-herd size, which is currently at a multi-decade low."

Gunthorp said the problem should have been tackled decades ago by previous administrations, but that doesn't mean trying to fix it today won't harm consumers or ranchers.

"Once you fix the problem that should have been attacked 30 years ago, it's gonna cause somebody pain," he said. "It's gonna cause the consumer pain [or] the rancher pain. Maybe both."

Fox News Digital reached out to the USDA for further comment but did not hear back at time of publication.

item.title: Trump is fighting Iran with strategic clarity — and America is winning
item.description: Operation Epic Fury targets Iran's nuclear weapon sites, ballistic missiles, and proxy networks as unprecedented sanctions choke oil exports.
item.content:encoded:
Operation Epic Fury is the right war at the right time. And, informed by Bush and Obama/Biden administration failures, it is being fought in the right way.

Critics left and right make similar arguments: "Illegal war of choice," "unwinnable quagmire," "war makes the mullahs more extreme," and even "Trump is a Jewish puppet." These criticisms, and many who offer them, are detached from reality.

First, Epic Fury is a right and just war. Since 1979, the Islamic Republic of Iran has owed the American people a blood debt. But until now, American policymakers have generally failed to collect this debt, much less effectively manage the regime's ongoing threat to U.S. interests, regional peace and international economic stability. This is partly due to the regime’s dangerous "revolutionary" Islamic supremist ideology that drives Iran’s aggression against the United States and Israel; justifies its brutal internal repression and foreign adventurism, including massive investments in the Hamas, Hezbollah, Houthi, and Iraqi terrorist groups; and drives its development of advanced offensive ballistic missile, drone, and nuclear weapon capabilities. A rational actor would not spend billions subsidizing terror tunnels and missiles in Gaza and Lebanon when its own citizens lack clean water and reliable electricity. But the mullahs, like other "revolutionary" authoritarians, have different incentives.

IRAN IS NOT A NORMAL NATION YOU CAN MAKE DEALS WITH; IT’S A NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT

Second, Epic Fury was launched at a uniquely favorable time because the regime has never been weaker.

Historically, the mullahs relied on geography, oil revenue and regional proxies for strategic deterrence. U.S. and allied diplomatic and military options were constrained by the possibility that the regime could close the Strait of Hormuz and disrupt international oil supplies, and by the fact that the utility of our economic sanctions were cabined by the robust commercial demand for Iranian oil and the political influence of the nations and networks that moved Iranian money. The Islamic Republic’s proxies, Hamas, Hezbollah, the Houthis, and Bashar al-Assad’s dictatorship in Syria, shielded Iran from its regional foes.

DISTRESS CALL CAPTURES TANKER UNDER FIRE, IRAN SHUTS HORMUZ TRAPPING THOUSANDS OF SAILORS

But President Donald Trump’s American energy dominance policy and rejuvenated U.S. military have essentially rendered Iran’s geography and oil resources a strategic nullity. Similarly, the regime’s proxy shield has been undone. Israel convincingly defeated Hamas and Hezbollah, then decimated Iran’s military and scientific leadership and fatally degraded the regime’s strategic air defense capabilities in the June 2025 "12 Day War." Assad fell, and the Houthis yielded to a combination of American resolve and punishing military strikes. And thanks to the U.S. blockade, economic sanctions, and strong diplomatic engagement with the Gulf Arab states and China, the Iranian economy is rapidly collapsing. The mullahs have been left naked and bare.

Third, this war is being fought the right way.

Writing for Tablet magazine, the commentator Michael Doran describes the president as steering between "two wrecks" — the first, George W. Bush’s regime-change war in Iraq, and the second, Obama/Biden’s appeasement program of paying the mullahs for quiet, indulging their regional and nuclear aspirations, preventing Israel from dealing hard blows to Hamas and Hezbollah, and calling it peace.

Doran is generally correct.

FINISH THE JOB: WHY A HALF WAR WITH IRAN IS THE MOST DANGEROUS OUTCOME

Epic Fury is certainly not the Global War on Terror. Epic Fury has strategic clarity: The president has made it clear Iran will not have a nuclear weapon, will not threaten international shipping, and will not, directly or through proxies, attack other states in the region. Accordingly, the United States and its allies have focused on eliminating imminent threats posed by Iranian missiles, naval forces, nuclear infrastructure, and the security apparatus that enables proxy terrorism, while decapitating the regime’s leaders and maintaining crippling pressure through unprecedented maritime interdiction and financial sanctions. Success is measured by killing the enemy, destroying his ability to attack Americans and our allies and partners, and terminating the economic sources of his war machine. No American forces are tasked with reconstructing Iranian society or reconciling its factions.

By contrast, the GWOT was crippled by incoherence in its target, means, and ends. Even the GWOT’s name was nonsensical, employing the word "terror" as a euphemism for Islamic radicalism. On the ground, political "nation-building" objectives expanded without clear connection to the strategic goal. American forces, tasked with responsibility for local governance and security, were left to endure two decades of combat under crippling and ineffective rules of engagement. After more than 7,000 American deaths, 50,000 American wounded, and over five trillion in American taxpayer spending, the end was not democracy and social change in the Middle East, it was Biden’s Afghanistan retreat.

ROUND ONE OF IRAN FIGHT WENT TO THE US MILITARY. BUT ENDING THINGS IS MUCH HARDER

Epic Fury is also most assuredly not a continuation of the failed and morally bankrupt Obama/Biden appeasement policies: President Trump has acted decisively and effectively to ensure Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. The Obama/Biden policy was to pave the way for the Iranians to develop such a device and provided sanctions relief and other payments as they went along.

Operation Epic Fury is strategically sound and magnificently executed. America has air supremacy. Much of the Islamic Republic’s political and military leadership is dead. Layered defensive networks have significantly mitigated the threat from Iranian ballistic missiles and drones and the blockade of vessels bound for or departing Iranian ports has choked Iranian oil exports and commercial trade. Treasury’s "Economic D-Day" has put into place unprecedented secondary sanctions targeting the mullah’s bankers, digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping severing every economic lifeline that sustains the Iranian regime and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. And at every step, the Trump Administration’s close cooperation with Israel and our other regional friends and partners has been a significant force multiplier.

History teaches that the end phase of war against a fanatical, despotic enemy is difficult and unpredictable. But President Trump has proven that he, uniquely, has the courage to stay the course and the will to finally settle the mullahs’ account. The truth is this: The United States is winning.

item.title: The world is debating sanctions against Israel. I am watching young warriors rebuild their lives
item.description: Amid West Bank boycotts, Beit Halochem's wounded warriors receive prosthetics, PTSD support, scholarships, and vocational training across Israel.
item.content:encoded:
Last week the British government banned imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, and the foreign secretary told Parliament that London should have moved sooner. Eleven other countries signaled they would follow. 

In response, Israel barred a group of British lawmakers and ordered the U.K. consulate in east Jerusalem closed. You can argue that policy either way, and people will do that for months.

Let me be honest about my own reaction. I was not surprised.

Not by Britain. Not by the countries lining up behind it. Not by the language that arrived with it. I have spent enough time in this line of work to know when the mood turns, it turns in many places at once. It has turned in London and Paris and Sydney. It has turned on American campuses and in American arenas. It has turned in the comment sections under stories about my organization that have nothing to do with politics at all, stories about a man learning to walk again.

BRITAIN’S DRAMATIC CRACKDOWN ON ISRAELI SETTLEMENTS SPARKS FIERCE RESPONSE AS US BLOWBACK LOOMS

So I am not going to spend this column cataloging the hate. Others do that work well. I want to tell you what I deal with instead, because it is the better story and it is the more important one.

Here is my week.

There are more than 90,000 IDF disabled veterans, creating the largest rehabilitation effort in Israel's history. Since Oct.7 and through "Swords of Iron," the number of wounded warriors has grown faster than at any point since 1948, and they are younger than any generation before them. 

Most were called up as reservists and were wounded while serving in the reserves — they had a business to run, a thesis to finish a baby at home. Now many carry a psychological injury alongside the physical one — which means nobody in the parking lot can see it at all.

A 24-year-old who loses a leg is not just facing a hard year. He is facing sixty years of prosthetics, revisions and physical therapy, alongside a marriage, a mortgage and a career he fully intends to have. In my field, a lifetime is not a figure of speech.

‘NO JEWS, NO NEWS’ STRIKES AGAIN AS SELECTIVE COVERAGE OF THE 'UNSETTLERS' FUELS ANTI-ISRAEL ANGER

People assume this makes me bitter about the boycotts and the sanctions and the noise. It does not. It makes me impatient with it, which is different. The argument has become the one place where everyone participates and nothing gets built.

I care about words, by the way. Enormously. Just not those.

SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER

We keep a terminology guide in our organization and we enforce it. We do not say disabled soldiers. After injury, a person is a "Wounded Warrior", a "Zahal Disabled Veteran," a Beit Halochem member. 

We do not say a veteran suffers from PTSD. He is coping with it, living with it and the gap between those verbs is the gap between a man defined by an injury and a man managing one. We never say returning to normal life, because that phrase quietly informs a 24-year-old that his real life ended on a Tuesday in October and everything after is a consolation prize. We say rebuilding their lives, because that is precisely what is happening in front of me.

That is what careful language is for. Not winning an argument with a stranger online — it's handing a person back their dignity.

And the rebuilding is the story nobody is fighting over, which is the real scandal, because it is the best story available.

At Beit Halochem, the nationwide network of rehabilitation centers in Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, Haifa, Beer Sheva and Ashdod, the swimming pool is full by seven in the morning. 

A rehabilitation journey starts in that water and does not end there. Psychological support and treatment, delivered without shame and without a two-year wait. Vocational training and scholarships, because a man who cannot return to his trade needs a new one.

Programs for spouses and their children, who carry this too. Sport at a serious level, which is why so many of Israel's Paralympic athletes come out of these gyms. And a room full of people who have been exactly where you are and who will not let you vanish into your apartment.

A Beit Halochem member who could not raise his arm in January hung a medal around his daughter's neck in June. A warrior living with PTSD spoke for the first time to a circle of men who understood him before he finished the sentence.

Those are not miracles. Those are Tuesdays.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

After 75 years as Beit Halochem USA, we recently became "Warriors of Israel." That is not a marketing exercise. It is the plainest description of the people we serve and of what they are still doing at seven in the morning. Our promise is four words: their sacrifice, our responsibility.

Americans ask me constantly what they can do about the headlines. Arguing on the internet is not the only option available to you, and it is not the most useful one.

Boycotts are subtraction. A government can ban a crate of produce but no government on earth can ban a young man learning to swim again, and no one has yet found a way to sanction a scholarship, a prosthetic socket or an hour with a therapist. Those things get built, or they do not, and that depends entirely on whether people decide to build them. In a story where almost nothing is within your control, that part is.

The pool opens at seven. It will be full again tomorrow.

item.title: Trump brings new heat to controversial UN agency as alleged Hamas ties engulf scores of employees
item.description: UN Watch says UNRWA completed at most 13 of 50 reforms, accusing the agency of counting draft policies and pilot programs as finished overhauls.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump recently amplified a report about a U.S. government investigation that referred more than 100 current or former UNRWA employees over alleged ties to Hamas — as a new watchdog report accuses the U.N. agency of overstating how much it has reformed.

The scrutiny, which included Trump sharing the report on Truth Social in August, comes as Geneva-based UN Watch released a report Monday challenging UNRWA’s claim that it has completed 41 of the 50 reforms recommended by an independent review led by former French Foreign Minister Catherine Colonna.

UN Watch says that when it compared UNRWA’s claims with what Colonna actually recommended, at most 13 of the 50 reforms had been completed as prescribed. The group argues that UNRWA repeatedly counted drafting policies, launching pilot programs or creating plans as completed reforms even when full implementation had not occurred.

UN AGENCY ACCUSED OF HAMAS TIES SEES ANOTHER EUROPEAN NATION CUT FUNDING

"UNRWA is grading its own homework — and giving itself credit for reforms that exist mainly on paper," UN Watch Executive Director Hillel Neuer told Fox News Digital. "A policy is not a reform if it is ignored, unenforced or blocked by staff unions dominated by Hamas."

Among the examples cited in the report is staff vetting. UNRWA lists a "Commercial Vetting Pilot & Costed Plan" as completed, along with other screening measures. UN Watch argues that a pilot and implementation plan do not amount to a fully operational outside vetting system.

The report also challenges UNRWA’s education reforms. UNRWA lists systematic textbook reviews and randomized classroom inspections among completed steps, while a policy prohibiting problematic educational content is still described as "in progress."

Colonna herself said when presenting her review in April 2024 that some educational content remained problematic, citing "glorification of jihad," incitement to violence and maps that did not show Israel, while calling for a zero-tolerance approach.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS MORE THAN $1B IN UN BUDGET CUTS AS REFORM PUSH GAINS MOMENTUM

Pressed by Fox News Digital at Tuesday’s U.N. briefing over who independently verifies whether the reforms are actually working on the ground, U.N. spokesman Stéphane Dujarric defended the process.

"It is not just checking boxes for the sake of checking boxes," Dujarric said, "It’s about the implementation of those things."

Dujarric said UNRWA regularly reports to the General Assembly, holds integrity meetings open to member states and gives governments opportunities to scrutinize what the agency is doing.

WATCHDOG DEMANDS APOLOGY AFTER UN MEMORIAL ERRONEOUSLY HONORS HAMAS TERRORIST

Asked specifically about staff screening, he said UNRWA relies in part on countries where it operates.

"We rely on the member states also, where we operate, who have the capacity to check people to do so," Dujarric said, adding that UNRWA shares staff lists with Israeli, Jordanian, Lebanese and Syrian authorities. "If there are concerns, they need to be shared directly with UNRWA. When they are, they take action."

The Colonna review was commissioned by U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres in February 2024 after allegations that UNRWA employees had participated in the Oct. 7 attacks. Guterres accepted all 50 recommendations in April 2024 and agreed with UNRWA leadership to establish an action plan to implement them.

Neuer rejected the idea that the disagreement is merely about terminology.

"This is not a semantic disagreement over the meaning of ‘completed,’" he said. "UNRWA says the job is done, yet teachers tied to terrorist organizations remain in classrooms, Hamas-dominated unions obstruct discipline, and children continue to be exposed to incitement. Those are real-world consequences, not technicalities."

item.title: MLB's most electric slugger just had one of the slowest, most disrespectful walk-off home runs of all time
item.description: Junior Caminero's 41st homer sealed a 2-1 Rays win over the A's, but his 40-plus-second home run trot stole the show and sparked AL MVP talk.
item.content:encoded:
Tampa Bay Rays phenom Junior Caminero is making a serious run at the AL MVP, but all fans saw Tuesday night was quite possibly the slowest walk of all time.

Maybe this is what hitting a "walk-off" home run truly means? I don't know. If so, the 23-year-old nailed it.

EX-MLB PITCHER GIVES HIS TAKE ON METS RELIEVER JEFRY YAN'S WILD STRIKEOUT SPLIT CELEBRATION

Caminero hit his second walk-off in the span of five days Tuesday against the A's, wrapping his 41st home run of the year around the right field foul pole to win the game, 2-1. The superstar slugger is now hitting .279 this season to go along with the 41 dingers, along with 96 RBI and a nearly .900 OPS.

For most of the season, the AL MVP has been Yordon Álvarez's to lose. And the Houston slugger hasn't lost it, by any means.

But Caminero is on the verge of ripping it away — and his home run trot after Tuesday's walk-off may have sealed the deal.

Take a look:

Goodness gracious. I grew up watching David Ortiz absolutely milk home run trots, but I'm not sure I've ever seen one quite like that. Are you even allowed to touch the runner before he hits home? They're all just high-fiving him down the first base line.

We grew up being SCOLDED if we dared touch a batter before he touched home. It was basically a sin.

Apparently, that's just a myth — at least in the MLB rulebook. A deeeeeeeep dive actually revealed that there is no rule in MLB on this, but it's actually pretty strictly enforced down in the college ranks.

ASTROS PLAYER BELTS HOME RUN, ROUNDS THE BASES AND THEN GETS DEVASTATING NEWS AFTER TOUCHING HOME

Rule 5, Section 2 states: After a home run, no offensive team member, other than the base coaches, shall touch the batter-runner before home plate has been touched.

No such rule exists in Major League Baseball. True story. The more you know!

Anyway, Caminero's blast gave the Rays their 91st win of the year. Tampa has already clinched a playoff spot, and will likely wrap up the AL East here in a few days.

As for the 40+ second trot, most on social media loved it. Some, of course, want him drilled in the ribs in the first inning tonight.

item.content:encoded:

In total, the head coach uttered the phrase five times before finally getting Howes' attention and asking him how he was doing. Franklin was clearly just trying to be nice, but that doesn't mean the moment wasn't also cringeworthy.

item.title: iOS 27 is here: 10 iPhone features you’ll want to try now
item.description: Safari's Notify Me can monitor websites for price changes and restocks, while new AI photo tools let you reframe and extend shots in iOS 27.
item.content:encoded:
Your iPhone is getting a major update. Apple released iOS 27 to the public on Monday, Sept. 14, bringing a wave of new features along with the long-awaited Siri AI beta.

However, there is much more happening under the hood. Safari can now watch websites for changes. The Photos app gets powerful new editing tools. Apple also says it has made iOS faster across compatible iPhones.

Some of these changes could save you from digging through apps or hunting for information yourself. Others give you more control over how your iPhone looks and works. Here are the iOS 27 features I think are worth trying first, along with how to find them.

NEW! Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better healthcare With AI

In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you take a more active role in your healthcare. You’ll learn how to organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare questions for your next doctor’s visit. No technical experience is needed.

Register for free now at CyberGuyLive.com.

8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT

The good news is that Apple kept support fairly broad. iOS 27 works with the iPhone 11 family and newer models. It also supports the second-generation iPhone SE and later. That means plenty of people can upgrade without buying a new phone. However, the biggest AI features have tougher hardware requirements. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI require an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 15 Pro Max, or an iPhone 16 model or later. So, an iPhone 11 can run iOS 27, but it will miss Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features.

Keep in mind that many of the features below, including the new AI photo tools, Safari Notify Me and Call Context, also require an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone. Siri AI is rolling out in beta in English on supported devices. Apple says support for additional languages will follow later. Availability can also vary by region.

Apple says iOS 27 brings performance improvements across the system. In Apple's testing, apps can launch up to 30% faster, new photos can load in the Photos app up to 70% faster and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% faster. Apple also says iOS 27 improves transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular connections and makes Mail search more relevant. Those are Apple's own figures, so your results will vary depending on your iPhone and how you use it.

Before installing a major update, I recommend backing up your iPhone. Also, connect to Wi-Fi and make sure you have enough battery life or plug your phone into power.

Then follow these steps:

If iOS 27 does not appear immediately, check again later. Apple software releases can take some time to appear on every compatible iPhone.

Apple Intelligence moves deeper into the Photos app with Spatial Reframing. It lets you change the composition and perspective of a photo after you took it. Apple Intelligence can generate additional parts of the scene when your new framing exposes areas that were outside the original shot.

Because AI may create new portions of the scene, I would zoom in and inspect the result before sharing an edited photo. Generative tools can still produce odd details.

Maybe you took a photo too close to your subject. The new Extend tool lets you expand beyond the original edges while Apple Intelligence generates the missing surroundings.

The feature will not work with every photo. Apple also says its intelligent photo-editing tools can be subject to daily usage limits.

Apple has also upgraded Clean Up in Photos. The tool can now tackle larger unwanted objects and distractions while using AI to fill in the space left behind.

This could be especially handy for removing a person in the background or another distraction that pulls attention away from the subject.

Apple is also giving Image Playground a major upgrade in iOS 27. You can now generate images in many more styles, including photorealistic ones. You can also start with an existing image and describe how you want Apple Intelligence to change it.

For example, you could ask it to change the setting or adjust the overall look without starting from scratch. As with Apple’s other generative image tools, usage limits may apply. I would also look closely at the results before sharing them, especially when people or detailed objects appear in the scene.

This may end up being one of my favorite iOS 27 features because it solves a very common frustration. Safari’s new Notify Me feature can monitor a webpage for a change you care about. For example, you could ask Safari to watch for a product coming back in stock. It can also monitor a page for a price change. Instead of reopening the same page over and over, Safari can alert you when something changes.

You can choose hourly, daily, weekly or monthly checks. However, Notify Me does not yet work on every website. Safari can also automatically organize open tabs by topic, which could help anyone whose browser looks like a digital junk drawer by the end of the week.

APPLE AI SECURITY UPDATE PROVES HACKERS MOVE FAST

Apple Intelligence is also getting involved when you call businesses. A new feature called Call Context can surface useful information from other apps while you are on a call.

Say you call an airline about a reservation. Call Context can pull up a confirmation code from Mail rather than forcing you to leave the Phone app and search for it while someone waits on the other end.

There is no complicated workflow to learn. When you place a supported business call and Apple Intelligence identifies relevant information, it can surface that information during the call.

Apple says its system determines what could be useful based on who you are calling. It can do that without analyzing the audio from your call. That is the kind of AI feature I want to see more of, because you do not have to change your behavior to benefit from it.

Last year, Apple introduced the transparent Liquid Glass design across iOS. Some people liked the new look. Others found certain screens harder to read. With iOS 27, Apple says it has improved contrast and readability. More importantly, you now have greater control over how transparent the interface appears. Apple added a slider that lets you move the look from ultraclear toward fully tinted.

The changes appear in real time as you move the slider. The setting applies across iOS, including places such as Control Center, notifications and app overlays. This is a small change, but I like that Apple is giving people a choice rather than assuming one visual treatment works for everyone.

If you are always digging around for the timer, exposure or another Camera setting, iOS 27 lets you keep the controls you use most right above the camera frame. Apple starts you with Flash and Live Photo there, but you can customize the row with other tools you use regularly.

Depending on your iPhone and camera mode, available controls can include Flash, Live Photo, Timer, Exposure, Styles and Aspect. Apple also gives you a Reset to Essentials option if you want to return to the default setup.

Apple has put a lot of work into parental controls in iOS 27. The new Ask to Browse feature lets a child request access to a website that has been restricted. The parent receives that request through Messages and can approve or decline it.

You first need Family Sharing set up with your child in the family group.

When your child tries to visit restricted web content, they can send an Ask to Browse request for your approval. Apple has also expanded Communication Safety. It already helps protect children from nudity in supported Apple services. With iOS 27, Apple says the system can intervene when it detects gore or violent content in shared photos and videos.

Find My gets a useful privacy upgrade in iOS 27, especially if you only want someone to see your location for a limited amount of time. You can now choose a custom duration for location sharing or set an exact date and time for it to stop. That could come in handy on a trip, during an event or anytime you want temporary location sharing without having to remember to turn it off later. You can also pause location sharing until the end of the day for specific people. Apple says this can be useful when you want to keep something like a surprise party or gift-shopping trip private.

If you already share your location with someone, you can also pause sharing with that person until the end of the day from their location-sharing options. I like having more control here because location sharing often makes sense for a specific situation. You may want someone to know where you are during a weekend trip without giving them indefinite access afterward.

Shortcuts can be incredibly powerful, but building one manually can get complicated fast. iOS 27 makes the process much easier with Describe a Shortcut. You can tell Apple Intelligence what you want your iPhone to automate in plain English. Shortcuts then connects the actions needed to build it. For example, Apple says you could ask your iPhone to message someone with your ETA when you leave work. You could also build automations that work across supported apps.

This could make Shortcuts much more approachable for people who have always liked the idea of automating their iPhone but never wanted to figure out how all the individual actions fit together. Some Shortcuts that rely on Apple’s cloud-based AI models may be subject to daily usage limits.

ASKED SIRI TO CALL YOUR BANK? A SCAM COULD COST THOUSANDS

This is the feature many iPhone owners have been waiting for, but I would treat it differently from the 10 features above. Siri AI is rolling out as a beta in English on supported devices, so expect some rough edges while Apple continues to improve it.

Siri AI can hold more natural conversations and handle follow-up questions. It can also use personal context from information on your device.

For example, you could ask Siri to find an old photo without remembering when you took it. You can also ask it to locate something buried in an email or note. Siri can take more actions inside apps, too. Apple says it can work across messages, emails, photos and other supported apps. Siri can also pull information from the web when you ask broader questions.

The real test will be whether Siri can save you from bouncing between apps. I have always found voice assistants most useful when they remove a few steps from something I already wanted to do. If Siri AI can reliably find a buried email or pull up a photo from years ago based on a vague description, that could change how often people use it. Because this is still a beta, I would double-check important answers or actions before relying on them.

Apple has also given Siri its own app, which makes it feel more like the AI assistants people have grown used to using.

You can also pin conversations you want to keep handy. Apple says you can invoke Siri AI by saying "Hey Siri," pressing the side button or swiping down from the Dynamic Island on supported iPhones.

What I like most about iOS 27 is that some of its best features solve problems you actually run into. Safari can keep an eye on a webpage so you do not have to. The new photo tools could rescue a shot you thought was unusable. Find My also gives you better control over how long someone can see your location. I am especially interested in what Apple Intelligence can do with Shortcuts. Describing an automation instead of building it action by action could finally make Shortcuts approachable for people who have always found it too complicated. Siri AI is still the feature I will be watching most closely. Apple is asking us to trust Siri with more personal context and more complicated requests, so getting the answers right will be critical. The fact that Siri AI launches as a beta tells me we should expect some bumps along the way. What I want from AI on my iPhone is pretty simple. Save me time without making me think about the technology doing the work. If iOS 27 can consistently do that, these features could become the ones you use every day without even thinking about them.

What would Siri AI have to prove before you let it handle more of your day? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.

item.title: NBC reporter, pilot among the victims identified in deadly Los Angeles helicopter crash
item.description: Journalist Eliana Moreno and pilot George Marciniw were identified as victims of the NBC4 helicopter crash in Los Angeles' Chatsworth neighborhood.
item.content:encoded:
Two victims of a deadly Tuesday night helicopter crash in Los Angeles have been identified as journalist Eliana Moreno and pilot George Marciniw, NBC4 Los Angeles confirmed.

Moreno and Marciniw were employees of Angel City Air, a helicopter charter company that operated NBC Los Angeles' NewsChopper4, NBC4 reported.

The pair were covering a deadly bus crash in downtown Los Angeles when the helicopter, which NBC4 confirmed belonged to the network, lost altitude and crashed, killing a third person on the ground who has yet to be identified.

ARMY IDENTIFIES 2 PILOTS KILLED IN APACHE HELICOPTER CRASH NEAR FORT HOOD DURING TRAINING EXERCISE

Moreno had been a stalwart of both NBC4 and Telemundo 52's aerial coverage for years, going by the moniker "Eli in the Heli."

She had worked closely with Marciniw since 2023, with the pair sharing social media photos of them working and dining together through the years.

Marciniw was, according to NBC4, a Southern California native who graduated from Burbank High School in 1974.

"We are deeply saddened to share that a helicopter providing aerial news coverage for NBC4 and Telemundo 52 was involved in a fatal accident in Los Angeles on Tuesday evening. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of those who lost their lives," NBC4 and Telemundo 52 said in a statement.

AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY AND STRIKES 'MULTIPLE' VEHICLES; 5 DEAD, 5 INJURED

The chopper crashed between two buildings in Los Angeles' Chatsworth neighborhood, producing a large fireball and injuring a fourth person.

The injured person was transported to a local hospital in unknown condition, Los Angeles Fire Department Capt. Branden Silverman told reporters.

"Our hearts are with the victims and families of tonight’s devastating Metro bus and helicopter crashes in Chatsworth, and with the entire NBC4 family," California Gov. Gavin Newsom wrote in a statement on X.

"Thank you to the first responders working tirelessly tonight," he added.

DATA SHOWS AMAZON JET’S KEY BRAKING SYSTEMS DID NOT DEPLOY DURING DEADLY MIAMI CRASH: NTSB

The National Transportation Safety Bureau (NTSB) and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said they will be sending investigators to the crash site on Wednesday to probe the crash's cause.
